clue.text: Note down something in bed

parts.note: F is a musical note, one of the letters naming notes of the scale
down as an adverb of direction means lower, further towards the ground

explanation.surface: An instruction to jot down an item found lying in one's bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note down' reads as 'write down', but it is two pieces. 'Something in bed' works twice: a bloom grows in a flowerbed, and a river (a thing that flows) runs in a riverbed, which sets up the puzzle's theme of flowers and rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Blooms are planted in garden beds, and a stream runs along its riverbed, so either sense lies in a bed.

clue.text: 1 across lets ya out, say

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is to be heard rather than read, its sound matching the answer

parts.note: lets out means frees, and ya is casual speech for you, giving frees ya

explanation.surface: Someone casually releasing a friend: 'lets ya out'.
explanation.definitionFit: This fragrant South African plant of the iris family is a popular garden and cut bloom.

clue.text: Bizarre off and on

parts.note: off in the sense of away or not on means out
re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Something strange that keeps switching off and on.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré, borrowed from French, describes behaviour or taste beyond what is usual, so eccentric or strange.

clue.text: 1 across risen, there's a cuckoo circling

indicators.note: circling says the scrambled letters go round the other piece
cuckoo means crazy, so the letters of these words are jumbled

parts.note: something risen is up

explanation.surface: A cuckoo flying in circles above a risen river.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 1 across is read as 'flow-er', a thing that flows, i.e. a river; Theresa is a girl's name, but the letters are just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as something that flows, the clue word becomes a river, and this one runs through Iraq to the Gulf.

clue.text: 1 across finding fault with bully

parts.note: to cow is to intimidate or bully
a slip is a small error or fault

explanation.surface: Someone criticising a bully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finding fault' looks like a single verb phrase, but fault is SLIP and bully is COW as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: This yellow spring wildflower of the primrose family grows in meadows.

clue.text: 1 across, hero missing rugby posts

indicators.note: missing says the posts' letter is lost from the hero

parts.note: a champion is a hero or defender of a cause
rugby goalposts are shaped like the letter H

explanation.surface: A rugby hero who keeps missing the posts with his kicks.
explanation.definitionFit: This pink or white wildflower of the pink family grows in hedgerows.

clue.text: 1 across gets to stitch up monarch

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to stitch is to sew
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

explanation.surface: A river helping to stitch up a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets to' is a link. Here 1 across means a river, read as a thing that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as something that flows, the clue word is a river, and this one runs through northern Germany past Bremen.

clue.text: Prided hair is on male that's wild, covering top of neck

indicators.note: covering says the jumbled letters surround the neck's first letter
wild signals letters going out of control into a new order
top of picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A wild male whose hair covers the top of his neck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges IS ON MALE to LIONSMAE, and N goes inside. 'Prided' means belonging to a pride of lions.
explanation.definitionFit: A pride is a group of lions, so the hair of a pride member is the male's mane.

clue.text: Study the country's economy, primarily

parts.note: Peru's: the country is Peru, with its possessive

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A call to study a nation's economy above all.
explanation.definitionFit: To peruse a document is to read it closely, which is to study it.

clue.text: Joint where tenor almost swallows piano

indicators.note: swallows says one piece takes the other inside it
almost says the last letter is cut

parts.note: Enrico Caruso was the great Italian operatic tenor
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A tenor at the piano, and a question of where a joint is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims CARUSO to CARUS, which then takes in P.
explanation.definitionFit: The carpus is the wrist, the joint between hand and forearm, made of eight small bones.

clue.text: Medium discharge, maximum in obstreperous camels

indicators.note: in says the maximum goes inside the jumbled camels
obstreperous means unruly, so the letters run riot

parts.note: top means maximum, as in top speed

explanation.surface: Unruly camels discharging at full strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' looks like a size or average; it is the spiritualist at a séance, and the scrambled camels give ECLASM before TOP goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Ectoplasm is the substance supposedly given off by a spiritualist medium during a séance.

clue.text: 1 across's Antarctic expedition?

parts.note: the Antarctic is in the far south, S
a tour is a journey or expedition

explanation.surface: A question about a polar expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 1 across means a river, a thing that flows; the 's stands for 'is'. The Stour is a river in southern England, the name shared by several English rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as something that flows, the clue word is a river, and several English rivers bear this name.

clue.text: Strongly maintain small 1 across

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
the clue word read as something that flows is a river, here the Wear in north-east England

explanation.surface: Insisting on a small bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wear is a river in north-east England, running through Durham.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear something is true is to assert it firmly, to maintain it strongly.

clue.text: 1 acrosses border river in places

indicators.note: in says the border and river go inside places

parts.note: poses means puts or places, as with a question
a rim is an edge or border
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Rivers bordering towns, as in a geography lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: These pale yellow spring blooms are among the commonest woodland wildflowers.

clue.text: A conspirator twisted at first, seeking plant

indicators.note: twisted at first says the first two letters change places

parts.note: Brutus was a conspirator in the murder of Julius Caesar

explanation.surface: A plotter seeking a plant after a twisted beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twisted at first' swaps the opening B and R of BRUTUS, giving RBUTUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The arbutus, or strawberry tree, is an evergreen shrub or tree with red berries.

clue.text: 1 across's bottom half set on a stool, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase is heard, not read, to give the answer

parts.words: bottom half set on a stool
parts.note: one buttock is half a bottom, and set on a stool puts it up, giving buttock up

explanation.surface: A question about half a bottom perched on a stool.
explanation.walkthrough: A bottom has two halves, so one half is a buttock; perched on a stool it is up. Said quickly in a British accent, buttock up sounds very like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This shiny yellow meadow bloom is a common wildflower of fields and lawns.

clue.text: 1 across having to kiss a redhead

parts.note: to neck is to kiss and cuddle
the head of red is its first letter, R

explanation.surface: A flower kissing a redhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 1 across means a river, a thing that flows: the Neckar is a German river through Heidelberg.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as something that flows, the clue word is a river, and this one flows through Stuttgart and Heidelberg.

clue.text: 1 across for motor race

parts.note: a motor is a car
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: A flower entered for a motor race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Motor race' looks like one idea but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This ruffled pink, red or white bloom is often worn as a buttonhole.

clue.text: The way to have a relative balance

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
sis, short for sister, is a relative

explanation.surface: Advice that relatives keep you balanced.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of equilibrium in which nothing changes, a balance of forces.

clue.text: 1 across being quiet in the year, forlorn ultimately

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
anno is Latin for in the year, as in anno Domini

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A quiet, forlorn flower in a hard year.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 1 across means a river, a thing that flows: the Shannon is Ireland's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as something that flows, the clue word is a river, and this one is the longest in Ireland.

clue.text: 1 across experienced UN's absence at the front

indicators.note: absence at the front says the letters go missing from the start

parts.note: underwent means experienced or went through
UN, the United Nations, with its possessive

explanation.surface: A flower that knew the United Nations was missing from the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 1 across means a river, a thing that flows: the Derwent is the name of several English rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as something that flows, the clue word is a river, and several in England are named Derwent.

clue.text: Man with a tough guy image ironed pants

definitions.text: Man with a tough guy image

indicators.note: pants as British slang for rubbish signals the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A tough guy who irons his trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like trousers; in British slang it means rubbish, so here it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert De Niro is the actor famed for playing hard men in films like Raging Bull and Taxi Driver.

clue.text: More than one vessel among sheep arrives

indicators.note: among says the vessels go inside the sheep

parts.note: a tup is a ram, a male sheep
urns are vessels, the plural matching more than one

explanation.surface: Pots placed among sheep as the flock arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb turns up means appears or arrives, as a guest might.

clue.text: Drink problem out of season, fate ensuing

indicators.note: ensuing says the fate follows the trimmed season
out of says the problem leaves the season

parts.note: summer is a season
a sum is an arithmetic problem
one's lot is one's fate or destiny

explanation.surface: A drinking problem out of season, with fate following.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of' takes SUM from SUMMER, leaving MER.
explanation.definitionFit: Merlot is a red wine grape and the wine made from it, so a drink.

clue.text: Tiredness certainly in use of retina?

indicators.note: in says certainly goes inside the reworked retina
use of the retina's letters means putting them to work in a new order

parts.note: yes means certainly

explanation.surface: Asking whether eye fatigue comes from using the retina.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled retina gives ETRAIN. The whole clue also reads as a definition: tired eyes come from overusing the retina.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyestrain is fatigue of the eyes from overuse, a kind of tiredness.

clue.text: 1 across, everyone can see, left in dump

indicators.note: in says the film rating and left go inside the dump

parts.note: a tip is a rubbish dump in British English
U is the British film rating for universal, suitable for all

explanation.surface: A flower left in a dump for everyone to see.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a tip is a rubbish dump, and U is the film certificate for a film anyone may watch.
explanation.definitionFit: This cup-shaped spring bloom grows from a bulb and is associated with Holland.

clue.text: 1 across more likely to win, leader dropping off

indicators.note: leader dropping off says the first letter is removed

parts.note: faster, in a race, means more likely to win

explanation.surface: A bloom more likely to win once the leader drops off.
explanation.definitionFit: This daisy-like bloom with starry petals flowers late in the year.

clue.text: Clip from Bardot, a serious stunner

indicators.note: Clip from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A film clip featuring a serious Brigitte Bardot, a beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is an electric weapon that stuns, so a stunner in the literal sense.

clue.text: Just around the corner, diet?

definitions.meaning: something just around the corner is nearby, in the neighbourhood
a diet food is ..., low in calories

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the word as 'lo-cal', short for low-calorie.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearby shops are neighbourhood ones, and low-calorie food is labelled lo-cal.

clue.text: 1 across one's to discover behind new line

indicators.note: behind says these pieces come after the new line

parts.note: an arc is a curved line
one's read as one is gives I plus is, here IS
to suss is to discover or work out

explanation.surface: A flower found behind a new line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' gives I + S, the 's standing for 'is'; with suss (to work out) they follow N and ARC.
explanation.definitionFit: This spring bloom, a daffodil relative, is named after the youth in Greek myth who loved his reflection.

clue.text: Skill of a tennis player pinches prize on the backhand?

indicators.note: on the backhand suggests hitting the other way, so the pieces read backwards

parts.note: nips means pinches
a pot is a prize or trophy, as in a cup

explanation.surface: A tennis player pinching a prize with a backhand shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the backhand' turns NIPSPOT round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Topspin is forward rotation a tennis player puts on the ball, a technique requiring skill.

clue.text: Open unimaginative starter, prawn cocktail

indicators.note: starter picks the first letter of the word before it
a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Complaining that the prawn cocktail is an unimaginative starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cocktail' mixes U (the first letter of 'unimaginative') with PRAWN.
explanation.definitionFit: To unwrap a parcel is to take off its covering, so to open it.
